hypothesis_change_reason: Materially different diagnosis, a different remedy, and it reverses the direction of the fix. Dispatch 127 concluded the project is 'stale', that the remedy is re-materialization from the live core root, and that the only thing standing in the way is the controller lock (release it, restart, done). This dispatch measured the provenance of the 16-file delta instead of its size. All 16 core-side sources of the delta are uncommitted working-tree modifications, and 16 of 16 of their blobs are absent from every commit on every ref of the core repository. Re-materializing therefore does not bring the project up to a canonical state; it binds a 61-wave program's canonical runtime to unreleased, unattested WIP. The controller lock is not the blocker and the proposed remedy is not the fix.

narrative.FINDING: The Agent Core project/core delta is not a missed release. It is unreleased work-in-progress that lives only in an uncommitted working tree of a different repository. The project's own 110 managed files are byte-for-byte the last released core state, so the project is not stale; the core is unreleased. All 7 red behaviours are tests that already exist in the released v1.0.0 validator, so the released core pair fails its own regression suite and the fix exists only as unattested WIP. This is a core-release defect in D:\Projeler\.agents-core, not a W57 defect, not a project defect, and not a defect that any project-side action can honestly repair.

narrative.HYPOTHESIS: If the project were 'stale with respect to a canonical core state', then the 16-file delta would consist of bytes that exist somewhere in the core's history. Measured instead, using the project's own guard pairing: all 16 are uncommitted core working-tree modifications, and not one of their blobs is present in any commit on any ref. The delta is therefore unattested WIP, and the project's correct state is the one it is already in.
narrative.CHANGE: Measurement only. No repository, core, manifest, lock or lifecycle file was written. (a) Re-ran the failing validator on this dispatch. (b) Re-ran W57's focused retest. (c) Re-ran the project's own guard with --core. (d) Drove materialization_guard.canonical_managed_targets(core) to obtain the authoritative 110 project/core pairs, then compared each project file against the live core source, and searched git rev-list --all for each delta source blob. (e) Compared each of the 16 project-side files against its v1.0.0 blob, raw and LF-normalised. (f) Located the 7 failing behaviours in both the released project validator and the core WIP validator. One new artifact plus .tmp scratch.
narrative.RESULT: Hypothesis confirmed and the previous remedy falsified. The project is at the release; the core is not. 16/16 delta sources are uncommitted, 16/16 delta blobs unattested in any core commit, 0/16 attested. 0 of the 16 project-side files differ from v1.0.0. The released v1.0.0 pair fails its own suite, and the fix is only in unattested WIP. Nothing in W57 can clear this, and re-materializing would import unreleased WIP into the canonical runtime of a 61-wave program.

measured_attribution.method: materialization_guard.canonical_managed_targets(D:\Projeler\.agents-core) gives the guard's own (canonical source, project-relative) pairs, 110 in total. This is the same pairing check_materialization uses, so the attribution cannot disagree with the guard. For each pair: sha256 of the project file against sha256 of the live core source (the guard's own comparison, no line-ending normalisation). For each delta pair: git hash-object of the live core source, then a search of git rev-list --all for a commit whose blob at that path equals it.

delta_project_side_vs_v1_0_0.conclusion: Every one of the 16 project-side files in the delta is the released v1.0.0 content. Combined with the 94 matching-and-attested pairs, all 110 project-managed files are the released state. The project is not stale.

true_owner_and_the_actual_remedy.owner: the Agent Core repository D:\Projeler\.agents-core (a different repository, with its own live controller pid 27300), and then the global bookkeeping owner (controller) for the project-side restart. Not W57, and not any Wave in this project.
remedy_sequence: 1. In the core repository: bring the 16 canonical-surface modifications to a committed, reviewed state (commit and tag, or revert). Until that happens there is no canonical state for any project to converge on, and the released v1.0.0 pair is known-red against its own suite.
2. Re-run the core's own validators on the committed state so the fix is attested before anything consumes it.

3. Only then re-materialize the project. Use the sanctioned entry point, not a bespoke transaction: .opencode/scripts/start-wave-program.ps1 already runs the guard at bootstrap (lines 316-323), performs the canonical materialization refresh on STALE (lines 329-353), re-verifies the guard (lines 355-360) and only then launches the controller (line 365). Restarting the program through it is the whole of the controller-side procedure; no manual lock surgery is required.
4. Rebind W57 evidence to the resulting content identity. Everything currently bound to 9c70d980... is superseded by the materialization.
true_owner_and_the_actual_remedy.why_a_phase_worker_cannot_do_this_and_wh: The worker cannot stop the controller it is running inside, and this dispatch's process ancestry was verified: pid 46004 -> 49016 (opencode serve) -> 10544 (opencode run) -> 56264 (run-ac-wave-opencode-phase.ps1 repair W57) -> 51592 (the live controller holding ac-wave-opencode-parallel.lock). But the lock is not the real constraint. The real constraint is that steps 1 and 2 are another repository's release decision. A worker that materialized around the lock would produce a green guard over unreleased WIP, which is worse than the honest red.
